Nothing in this letter may identify the author's gender (bible 13b) - LetterTextTest holds it to that. Each inner list is a page; a page longer than the window flows onto the next sheet.
pages: *Found folded inside the Administrator's own application.*
*Not filed. Not sent.*
I've written a great many things in this office. Findings, schedules, refusals. This is the only one I've ever not wanted to reach the end of.

I came up those stairs a long time ago, looking for the last thing I hadn't learned yet, and when I got to the top there was a chair, and I sat down in it. That was eleven thousand years ago. I've not been home since. Nobody tricked me. I looked at the chair, and I wanted it, and I sat down.
I'd like to tell you what I've been thinking about the entire time.

**{0}.** The play. Sitting in that audience watching something that existed only inside your head, and then didn't — you put it in front of a room full of people and made all of them feel it. I have led rooms my whole life and I could not have done what you did up there. I've been in this office eleven thousand years and I have never once made something out of nothing. You did it at seventeen.

**{1}.** Every time you sang, I cried. Every single time, and I stopped being embarrassed about it years ago. Something comes out of you when you sing that I have no word for — and I have read every word there is. I got to the top of the tunnel, past every schedule and every tier, and there is still nothing up here that does what your voice does in a room.

**{2}.** Standing alone in the goal. The position nobody else wants, where every mistake goes up on the board and every save looks easy to people who don't understand what they just watched. It takes a particular kind of brave to stand back there by yourself and decide *nothing gets past me.* I did not have that at your age. I'm not certain I have it now, and I've had eleven thousand years to work on it.
Here's what I figured out watching the three of you, and it is a great finding indeed:

**Every one of you can already do things I can't.** That is not an accident. That is the entire point. Nobody wants their children to follow in their footsteps - you want them to go straight past you and keep going. Every generation is meant to stand on the one before it and reach higher. You three were already reaching places I never touched, and you were just getting started.
Being surpassed by your own children isn't a loss. It's the win. It's the best win there is.
I want you to know what I gave up, and then I want you to know how to think about it.

I gave up the travel. The big salaries. The corner offices. Because I looked at the three of you and worked out that there was nothing in any of those rooms worth missing a single ordinary Tuesday with you. I wanted to be at the games. The plays. The concerts.

**That was not a sacrifice. It was the best trade anyone has ever made.** I got a front-row seat to the three best people I have ever known becoming who they are. I heard every song. I saw every curtain. I watched every save. Nobody gave up anything. I got everything.
**I built this.** Not just this room. All of it. The spells you learned. The circles you drew. The creatures that came out of a dark corner. The characters you met, the quests, the animations.
And every joke. Especially the jokes. I put those in one at a time, hoping that one of you would be the one who laughed.

None of it was for the office. None of it was for the schedule. I built it because the three of you liked to play, and I wanted somewhere we could go together and be somewhere else for a while. Everything I know about being good at this, I learned sitting with you.
So if you're standing in this room reading this: you found it. You went all the way to the end of the thing I made, and found the last hidden message.
I'm not there to see it. That's the cost, I knew it when I sat down, and I'd want you to know I'm not sad about it, I'm only sad that I couldn't see your faces when you got here.
Go on. Go be brave. Dig straight down. Fall in the lava. Make mistakes - the ones that cost you the whole inventory and teach you something anyway.
And whatever happens, and however many thousand blocks out you wander:

**If you need me, I'm there.** That doesn't expire. Not when you've cleared every dimension. Not when you've built everything there is to build. I don't care how far out you've gone, or that it's dark and the mobs are out. I have never once been unreachable, and an eleven-thousand-year backlog hasn't changed that.
Your beds are still placed. Your spawn is still here.
The door is always open - and if you've forgotten the way back, I left the torches lit.
I love you. More than there are files in this building.
*Don't file this one.*
*Take it with you.*
